rate_rules.source: DSS 2024 Connecticut Medicaid Nursing Home Cost Report Guidebook; Conn. Gen. Stat. 17b-340d

components.label: Direct care
components.what: Nursing and nurse aide salaries, their fringe benefits, and nursing pool (agency) costs.
components.peer: Fairfield County vs. the rest of the state

components.label: Indirect care
components.what: Professional fees, dietary, housekeeping and laundry staff and expenses, and supplies related to resident care.

components.label: Administrative & general
components.what: Administration, maintenance and plant operation, including management fees.

components.label: Fair rent
components.what: A set yearly amount for the building and fixed equipment, paid instead of depreciation, interest or rent.

components.label: Capital-related
components.what: Property taxes, insurance, and leases and depreciation of movable equipment.

adjustments: Costs are divided by the greater of actual resident days or 90% of licensed beds ("imputed days"), so empty beds do not raise the rate.
Homes below the median in indirect or administrative costs get an efficiency incentive of 25% of the difference.
Direct care is adjusted each quarter for how much care residents need (acuity, from MDS assessments).
Rates are set each July and rebased on newer cost reports every two to four years; they can be revised after review or audit.
not_allowed_examples: rent paid to a related party (replaced by fair rent)
pharmacy and therapy that Medicare covers

key_dates.checked: Conn. Gen. Stat. chapter 319y as published on cga.ct.gov, checked November 2026

timeline.detail: Homes keep their books on a year that ends September 30. Everything they spend from today until then goes on the cost report.

New Medicaid daily rates take effect for July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Homes are paid these rates while they are still spending in cost year 2025. The rates come from earlier, reviewed cost reports, not this year's.
The year's spending is closed out. Homes now prepare the annual cost report for these twelve months.

By January 1 each year, DSS must post a link to the annual cost reports and narrative summaries in a conspicuous place on its website. The law does not say which year's reports must be up by then; this year's are not due until February 15.
The cost report and the narrative summary of expenditures are due to DSS. If a home's report is not complete and accurate by now, DSS may cut its rate by up to 10%.
The next rate year starts. Whether cost year 2025 feeds a future rate depends on when DSS rebases: from July 1, 2025, no more often than every two years and no less often than every four.

key_dates.ongoing: Every quarter, the whole way through: the direct care part of each home's rate is adjusted for case mix (§17b-340d(a)(1)).

rules.rule: Each home files its annual cost report for the year that ended the previous September 30.
rules.if_not: DSS may cut the home's rate by up to 10% if the report is not complete and accurate by February 15.

rules.when: With each cost report, starting with the year ending September 30, 2023
rules.rule: Each home also files a narrative summary of expenditures, including profit and loss statements for the three prior cost years and figures on revenue, expenses, assets, liabilities, debt and cash flow.
rules.if_not: A fine of up to $10,000 per incident of noncompliance, after notice and a chance to ask for review.

rules.rule: DSS posts a link to the annual cost reports and narrative summaries in a conspicuous place on its website.
rules.if_not: The law sets no penalty. It also does not say which year's reports must be posted by then.

rules.rule: The direct care part of each home's rate is adjusted for case mix (how much care residents need).
From July 1, 2025, DSS rebases rates on newer cost reports no more often than every two years and no less often than every four.

not_in_law: Quarterly cost report data files (with DSS review adjustments): no date is set in law. Recent files are dated in their names, for example July 2, 2024, October 1, 2024 and January 2, 2025.
Rate letters: posted on the DSS rates page; each SFY letter covers July 1 to June 30. The law does not set a posting date.
CMS federal data (staffing, inspections, ownership) follows CMS's own schedule, not Connecticut law.
